title: Public Scopes
summary: Local-to-public payload flow and management-isolation guarantees for public read-only Docs Viewer routes.
content_html:
Docs Viewer Public Scopes

A public scope is locally managed canonical content delivered through a fixed read-only static route. It shares reader code with /docs/, but it does not share the management entrypoint, local service configuration, or local published-data source.

Data Flow

canonical Markdown
docs-viewer/scopes/<scope>/source/documents/
          |
          | build / local write follow-through
          v
local published docs + search
docs-viewer/scopes/<scope>/published/
          |
          | explicit Publish
          v
tracked public snapshots
site/assets/data/
          |
          v
fixed public static route
site/<route>/index.html

confirmed canonical document Delete
          |
          | exact negative cleanup
          v
tracked public snapshots

Canonical source is the authority. Local published data is the management and review surface. Public snapshots are the files deployed for public reads. Publish does not deploy the site or mutate source; it copies the reviewed local docs/search projection and removes only exact paths owned by current publishability exclusions. Confirmed canonical document Delete separately removes any exact current public projection and affected inventories immediately.

Public And Management Boundaries

concern public route local /docs/ route
scope Fixed by public route config. Selected from configured scopes.
runtime entrypoint Public only. Management contributions load after local context is established.
data reads Public site/assets/data/ snapshots. Local published-data service reads.
services No local service base URLs. Loopback Docs Viewer service.
controls Reader controls only. Capability-gated editing, import, publish, and lifecycle controls.
query state scope and management mode cannot widen the route. scope, doc, and supported management state are meaningful.

The static shell identifies a public route id and loads site/docs-viewer/config/routes/docs-viewer-public-routes.json. That browser-safe registry fixes the scope, viewer base URL, published payload URLs, and public UI features. The public viewer config is a filtered projection and contains no localhost management base URLs.

UI absence is not the sole security boundary. Public routes cannot load the management entrypoint, and mutation endpoints remain available only from the loopback service.

Publish Workflow

For a configured public scope, local management exposes one Publish command through the toolbar and Actions menu.

  1. GET /docs/publish/status compares local and public payloads.
  2. POST /docs/publish/confirm returns the proposed copy/remove diff without writing.
  3. POST /docs/publish/apply requires confirm: true and recomputes the operation before synchronizing files.

Publish reports changed plus excluded. Exclusions come only from surviving canonical documents carrying the current explicit publishable: false gate, including parent-owned descendants and required host consequences. Public files merely missing from source are retained and unreported; supported document Delete has already cleaned its own current public projection.

After those public files commit, Publish checks private lineage rows for configured Editorial sub-scopes. An exact public by-ID file sets that current Editorial child's published_url; an absent public by-ID file clears it. This private follow-through adds no browser payload, Publish option, receipt field, timestamp, generation digest, or publication history.

Local scopes do not advertise a public docs/search target. Their generated JSON remains under Docs Viewer-owned local published roots and must not be redirected into public site/assets/data/ paths.

Confirmed Document Delete

For a configured public parent or child collection, Delete preview derives exact current public impact from the public snapshot. Confirmed apply commits the canonical deletion and normal working rebuild first, then removes only exact by-ID and owned Mermaid products, filters affected tree, Recent, search, manifest, and document-location products, and requires affected Catalogue document URLs to refresh before success. A report-host Delete removes its routes and derived child URLs without inferring ownership of surviving child files. Local collections have no public cleanup, and an already-unprojected public document is a no-op at this stage.

Delete does not call Publish, copy pending Working edits, promote new documents, or remove shared media. For a configured lineage collection, exact Working or Editorial follow-through occurs only after the canonical mutation and any required public cleanup succeed: Working Delete removes its complete private record, while Editorial Delete removes only that child and any resulting empty record. A later ordinary Publish is idempotent for the completed public removal.

Public Payload Contract

Public routes read compact scope-owned files:

  • index-tree.json for publishable public navigation
  • recent.json for the small route-configured Recent list
  • by-id/<doc_id>.json for rendered document content and public-safe metadata
  • the scope search index.json

Public per-document payloads intentionally omit management metadata such as parent paths, publishability, UI status, internal route details, and report/service data. Search and public tree generation exclude non-publishable documents, while local management can still inspect their private generated payloads.

Public routes declare whether Recent means added or edited. The builder prepares that public projection independently and applies public visibility before its limit; Publish copies the prepared projection rather than trimming the local management list. Public Moments currently uses added, while Library and Analysis use edited.

Exact schemas belong to Generated Data Contracts and the builders/tests, not this boundary summary.

Creating And Deleting Public Scopes

Scope Lifecycle creates a public scope by writing its conventional source/config records, rendering a tracked static route shell, adding public and management route records, building local output, and copying the initial public snapshots.

The lifecycle manifest records the created route shell, source/output roots, and published payloads. Delete may remove them only for a scope recorded as user-created and tool-created. Shared runtime, CSS, templates, and route registry files are changed or reused; they are never recorded as deletable scope assets.

Executable Assurance

public_docs_viewer_readonly.py boots public routes from a static site root and verifies:

  • public app kind with management and source service disabled
  • no local service base URLs or management controls
  • the public route registry and public payload URLs are used
  • management query state is normalized away
  • only public-safe metadata appears in the info panel
  • tree, recent, document, search, and public report paths remain functional

Lifecycle tests separately prove that creating a public scope produces its route/config/payload set and that deleting an eligible scope removes only its owned records and files. Focused public Delete cleanup tests prove exact parent, descendant, child, report-host, location, Catalogue, local no-op, already-unprojected, and next-Publish behavior.

Extension Method

Add a public scope through lifecycle rather than hand-assembling a route. A change to the public delivery model should preserve four independent checks:

  1. canonical source and local published outputs remain outside site/assets/
  2. Publish is the explicit positive local-to-public synchronization boundary; confirmed document Delete owns only exact negative cleanup
  3. the public route loads only public-filtered config, payloads, and entrypoint modules
  4. browser smoke proves the absence of management/service state as well as successful reading

Weak Spots

  • Local and public payloads can intentionally differ until Publish; lineage-enabled editorial documents retain only their current private public URL, not automatic deployment or a publication-history ledger.
  • Public route and viewer configs are generated projections from canonical registries. Manual edits can create drift until builders or lifecycle rewrite them.
  • Media publication is configured per media type and is independent of the docs/search Publish diff; a location may use a local directory or R2 without changing the route's public/read-only classification.
  • Public isolation is layered across config filtering, route policy, entrypoint imports, capability absence, payload filtering, and loopback authorization. A change crossing those layers needs more than a UI visibility test.
  • Lifecycle artifact tests and public browser smoke are separate; a newly created route is not booted end to end in the same test.
